newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: DMG raises Argentine GDP growth estimates.
newsitem.headline: DMG raises Argentine GDP growth estimates.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Thursday that it had raised its estimate for growth in Argentine gross domestic product in 1996 to 3.6 percent from 3.0 percent.
It said it had raised its estimates for GDP growth in 1997 to 4.9 percent from 4.0 percent and for growth in 1998 to 4.3 percent from 4.0 percent.
"This across-the-board upgrade is supported by a more optimistic view in terms of domestic consumption, although investment and exports still remain the most dynamic components of demand," DMG said.
Other factors in the revision included recently revised government figures for second-quarter GDP growth.
Argentina's unemployment rate should decline to 16 percent or lower in 1997, and to 14 percent in 1998 from the current 17.3 percent, DMG said.
"Argentina registers a solid and sustained economic growth supported on investments and exports," it said.

It added, "Argentina is in a position to take full advantage of three important domestically driven factors: a strong investment drive in fixed assets, increases in productivity triggered by the structural reforms undertaken by the government during the 1990s, and substantial increases in domestic capital markets due to the start of the private pension funds and a deep turnaround in banking."
DMG said it continued to recommend stocks in sectors linked to investment and exports, such as oil, steel, and food, as well as banks.
